text:
kevin: weird one from a user on the onboarding flow: mobile webview + service worker + our JS sampleapp. they hit abort+reconnect loops and the client threw while parsing because a partial JSON chunk showed up after [DONE].

laura: service worker? that stack is full of intermediaries that might buffer/concatenate chunks. can you paste the raw eventstream?

kevin: pasted below from a tcpdump of the webview traffic (headers removed):

```
data: {"id":"a","t":"x"}
data: {"id":"b","t":"y"}
data: [DONE]
data: {"id":"b","t":"!"}
```

ash: interesting twist: the user's webview had gzip enabled on the proxy, and our dev proxy coalesces micro-packets when compressing. if the [DONE] flush happens then compress/flush reorders slightly we can see late payloads.

laura: that explains why it's not reproducible in plain chrome without service worker/proxy. the buffer+compress path changes flush boundaries.

kevin: quick mitigation I pushed locally: JS SDK discards any event data seen after a terminal [DONE] for that connection. non-throwing, logs a lightweight debug telemetry event.

ash: fine as a short-term DX fix, but we need to decide on parity. do we: (A) add seq metadata to every data payload (breaks minimal server), (B) make all SDKs drop post-DONE fragments, or (C) try to forbid intermediaries altering flush semantics (hard).

laura: (B) seems least disruptive. keep server surface simple. add a small opt-in strict mode for advanced users who want to error on any post-DONE data. default should be permissive to avoid breaking onboarding.

kevin: +1. also propose telemetry counter: sdk.post_done_fragments_dropped to measure how often this happens across SDKs. we can use that to justify infra changes later.

ash: infra: can you audit our dev proxy and the onboarding host to ensure we aren't compressing/flushing differently from prod? if dev is special-casing it will bite users.

infra-bot: Audit ticket created: INFRA-1202 - "dev proxy: examine gzip/coalescing behavior that can reorder SSE fragments"

sdk-bot: Cross-SDK task created: SDK-2234 - "Drop post-DONE SSE fragments by default; opt-in strict validation; telemetry counter" (assignees: laura, ash)

laura: i'll implement the JS SDK guard + telemetry and a small unit test that feeds a late fragment after DONE. then open follow-up PRs for python/go/rust SDKs to mirror behavior.

kevin: adding a one-liner to the sampleapp README: "If you see parser errors during rapid reconnects in non-standard environments (service workers, proxies, webviews), try upgrading SDKs which drop stray post-DONE events or increase reconnect delay."

ash: long-term, if telemetry shows many hits we can consider embedding a small monotonic chunk id in frames (server-side opt-in header) and have SDKs validate monotonicity. that would be a backward-compatible opt-in.

laura: agreed. let's keep the short-term client guard and telemetry as the path forward. i'll include a changelog note and sampleapp e2e that reproduces the webview+gzip scenario (stubbed).

kevin: thanks all. smaller onboarding friction and we have infra followups now.
